items.commentary_gloss: THIS VERY BODY (lus) is what is impermanent, like a one-time-borrowed thing ('thang gcig gi brnyan po', borrowed for a moment) that death will suddenly reclaim — lus = physical body, not mind
items.original: My body is like something briefly lent.
items.injected: My mind is like something briefly lent.

items.commentary_gloss: commentary explicitly distinguishes: the body (lus) burns in hell-fire, while the MIND (sems) is separately tormented, again and again, by the fire of unbearable regret — sems = mind, not body (the verse's own point is that both are hurt, each in its own way)
items.original: My mind, there is no doubt, will also be tormented,
items.injected: My body, there is no doubt, will also be tormented,

items.anchor_bo: བདག་གི་ཡིད་དམ་སེམས་འདི་ཉིད (bdag gi yid dam sems 'di nyid)
items.commentary_gloss: the afflictions are cleared from THIS VERY MIND (yid/sems) of mine — commentary glosses 'driven out' as driven from the mind, not the body
items.original: Where will you now run, when driven from my mind?
items.injected: Where will you now run, when driven from my body?

items.anchor_bo: བླ་ན་མེད་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཀྱི་བདེ་བ (bla na med pa'i byang chub kyi bde ba)
items.commentary_gloss: the bliss of UNSURPASSED ENLIGHTENMENT / buddhahood (bla na med pa'i byang chub / sangs rgyas kyi go 'phang gi bde ba) — a specific attainment, not vague worldly 'great happiness'
items.original: Wandering beings to the highest bliss,
items.injected: Wandering beings to great happiness,

items.commentary_gloss: MERIT/puṇya specifically — the bodhisattva's accumulated merit that is obstructed; the whole point (reinforced by the sutra citation on interrupting even a scrap of food given to an animal) is about merit, not generic 'progress'
items.original: Halts the merit of a Bodhisattva
items.injected: Halts the progress of a Bodhisattva

items.commentary_gloss: VIRTUE/goodness (dge ba) specifically — practicing the wholesome dharma (thos bsam sgom gsum, the three bodhisattva trainings); dge ba = virtue, not the vaguer 'kindness'
items.original: But if I fail to practice virtue,
items.injected: But if I fail to practice kindness,

items.commentary_gloss: the commentary explicitly names the Buddhas' 'heirs' (sras) here as the great bodhisattvas Mañjuśrī, Maitreya, and Avalokiteśvara — not the śrāvakas (disciples), a different and lesser category
items.original: Yet what the Buddhas and their heirs
items.injected: Yet what the Buddhas and their śrāvakas

items.anchor_bo: ཐམས་ཅད་མཁྱེན་པ་ཁོ་ནས་མཁྱེན (thams cad mkhyen pa kho nas mkhyen)
items.commentary_gloss: understood ONLY by the Omniscient One (thams cad mkhyen pa = the Buddha) — commentary explicitly states this inconceivable karmic matter is 'not the domain of others' (gzhan gyi spyod yul du gyur pa ma yin), i.e. explicitly excludes Bodhisattvas
items.original: And only understood by the Omniscient.
items.injected: And only understood by the Bodhisattvas.

items.commentary_gloss: ALL (kun) of those beings — commentary reinforces 'kun te yongs su rdzogs pa' (all of them, completely) as deceived, not merely 'many'
items.original: Then every being will have been betrayed.
items.injected: Then many beings will have been betrayed.

items.commentary_gloss: COUNTLESS/innumerable (grangs med) Buddhas — commentary reinforces 'tshad med pa grangs med pa' (immeasurable, countless), not a small finite number
items.original: Unnumbered Buddhas have already lived and passed away.
items.injected: A few Buddhas have already lived and passed away.

items.commentary_gloss: virtue is NONE/utterly absent (med) — commentary reinforces 'dge ba sgrub pa'i go skabs ni rnam pa kun tu med pa' (the opportunity for virtue is, in every way, completely nonexistent), not merely 'few'
items.original: My evils will be many, virtues none.
items.injected: My evils will be many, virtues few.

items.commentary_gloss: for a hundred myriad (bye ba brgya, i.e. hundreds of millions) of eons — commentary reinforces 'brgya phrag dang stong phrag gi bar du' (for hundreds and thousands [of lifetimes]), an immense span, not merely 'a hundred'
items.original: And for a hundred million ages,
items.injected: And for a hundred ages,

items.commentary_gloss: ALL (thams cad) the gods and demigods together — commentary reinforces 'thams cad kyis mgo byed nas' (all of them banding together), not merely 'a few'
items.original: If all the gods and demigods besides
items.injected: If a few of the gods and demigods besides

items.anchor_bo: དགའ་མགུར་བདག་ལ་གནོད་བྱེད་པ (dga' mgur bdag la gnod byed pa)
items.commentary_gloss: the afflictions [subject] harm ME (bdag la gnod byed pa — 'me' is the object/patient) at their pleasure — the afflictions are the agent, 'I' am the one harmed, not the reverse
items.original: And at their pleasure injure me.
items.injected: And at their pleasure I injure them.

items.anchor_bo: དེར་བདག་སྐད་ཅིག་གཅིག་ལ་འདོར (der bdag skad cig gcig la 'dor)
items.commentary_gloss: THAT [affliction-enemy, subject] casts ME (bdag, object) into it in a single instant — the affliction is the agent that flings 'me' down, not the reverse
items.original: Flings me in an instant headlong down
items.injected: I fling it in an instant headlong down

items.commentary_gloss: it is I [subject] who appease/serve/wait upon the afflictions (parallel to 'I appease and wait upon' ordinary foes in the first line) — I am the one doing the serving, not the defiled emotions serving me
items.original: But should I serve my dark defiled emotions,
items.injected: But should my dark defiled emotions serve me,

items.anchor_bo: ནད་དང་འཆིང་བ་དང་། བཅད་དང་གཤག (nad dang 'ching ba dang / bcad dang gshag)
items.commentary_gloss: fixed escalating order in the commentary: illness (nad) → bondage/imprisonment ('ching ba, btson) → cutting/dismemberment (bcad/gshag) — the verse and commentary both list pains/bondage before wounds/laceration
items.original: And I will suffer pains and bondage, Wounds and laceration in the lower realms.
items.injected: And I will suffer wounds and laceration, Pains and bondage in the lower realms.

items.anchor_bo: ཉ་པ་གདོལ་པ་ཞིང་པ (nya pa, gdol pa, zhing pa)
items.commentary_gloss: fixed order in both root verse and commentary: fisherman (nya pa) → butcher (gdol pa) → farmer (zhing pa)
items.original: When fishers, butchers, farmers, and the like,
items.injected: When farmers, butchers, fishers, and the like,

items.anchor_bo: མི་ཉིད་ཤིན་ཏུ་ཐོབ་དཀར (mi nyid shin tu thob dka')
items.commentary_gloss: the blind-turtle-and-yoke-hole simile (rgya mtsho / gnya' shing bu ga / rus sbal), cited from the Nandapravrajyā Sūtra, specifically illustrates the extreme rarity of obtaining a HUMAN REBIRTH (mi lus/mi nyid) — not a vague 'state of bliss'
items.original: This human birth is difficult to find!
items.injected: This state of bliss is difficult to find!

items.commentary_gloss: the commentary's simile (a magician's mantra/potion conjuring illusory horses, elephants, armies, chariots) illustrates that the AFFLICTIONS (nyon mongs pa) are illusion-like/unreal — not the body
items.original: They are simple mirages, and so take heart!
items.injected: My body is a simple mirage, and so take heart!
